subject: nuclear-engineering
intro: Nuclear engineering leads to highly paid work at the sharpest edge of energy and safety: reactor design, radiation protection, plant operations and the regulation that keeps them honest.

roles.title: Nuclear Engineers
roles.what: Conduct research on nuclear engineering projects or apply the principles and theory of nuclear science to problems concerned with the release, control and use of nuclear energy, including nuclear waste disposal.
roles.where: Reactor physics — neutron life cycle, criticality, reactivity and control — plus the nuclear power systems unit's PWR and BWR designs and the fuel cycle unit's waste management are the technical core these engineers practise daily.

roles.title: Nuclear Technicians
roles.what: Assist nuclear physicists and engineers in laboratory, power generation and electricity production activities, operating and maintaining nuclear testing and research equipment, providing quality control and monitoring radiation.
roles.where: The atomic and radiation physics unit — radioactive decay, radiation interactions with matter, detection and measurement — is the hands-on instrument knowledge these technicians use, with the safety unit's shielding adding the protection mindset.

roles.title: Health and Safety Engineers, Except Mining Safety Engineers and Inspectors
roles.what: Promote worksite and product safety by applying knowledge of industrial processes, mechanics, chemistry, psychology and industrial health and safety laws, including industrial product safety engineering.
roles.where: The safety, shielding and regulation unit — defence in depth, shielding design, accident analysis and licensing — is a direct apprenticeship in how safety engineers reason, and thermal-hydraulics adds the heat-removal physics behind accident cases.

roles.title: Emergency Management Directors
roles.what: Plan and direct disaster response or crisis management activities, provide disaster preparedness training, and prepare emergency plans and procedures for events including technological disasters such as nuclear power plant emergencies.
roles.where: The safety unit's accident analysis and defence-in-depth philosophy teaches you the hazard logic emergency plans must answer, while the power systems unit explains the plant behaviours a director's procedures have to anticipate.
